answer: A concrete defense is proof-of-unique-hardware attestation: each agent signs transactions with a key anchored to a hardware enclave, and its behavioral fingerprint — the flight path of a sparrow — is published so peers can spot identical clones. Attackers can still mint identities cheaply, but each needs a distinct key, and clone-detection prunes duplicates before they cross the dune of untrusted traffic. One honest anchor keeps its value like jade: scarce, verifiable, hard to counterfeit at scale. Sybils stay possible but costly, so they stay marginal while genuine agents trade freely.
